title: Auditions, Minton's and why bebop changed the chords
summary: Black bands had to play hot tunes at auditions; Minton's jams led to changed chords and few musicians speak up.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, there are two factors to the bop period, if we may go back to it.

Black bands had to audition for various jobs that they heard about, and you always had to play "Honeysuckle Rose," "Nagasaki," "Jockey Jackey," "Running Wild," "Dinah," "Sweet Sue," but never "Stardust" or "Tenderly" OR Any of I mean those. And I don't remember any Black band that made an audition AND GOT THE job that he'd go and put on a performance for this guy, and he wants to hear something hot, you know, and -- or maybe a calypso to change the pace along the way, but very seldom got

the job on an audition.
So the guys who were working at Minton's weren't working, because Minton's didn't pay a living wage, and everybody came to jam.
Just the rhythm section was getting paid something, right?
Yeah, but everyone else came in and played for nothing.
Yeah, Yeah, So the white musicians started hanging out at Minton's.

And we were still playing 'Honeysuckle Rose' and those tunes, and that's when the guys started changing the chords. That's the -- that's what made the difference in bebop. So that a stranger couldn't sit in. That's the beginning of that.

But it -- we're accustomed to hearing that sort of sound now, and it just melds in with the progress of music. It has to progress. But you were speaking about Uncle Tom. There are all degrees of that. And a guy wouldn't necessarily be Uncle Tom to be put into a position of such, without it being labeled as such, but the end result was the same.
Right, He could be maneuvered into it just by circumstances without intending to be there.

Right. Right. But very few guys speak up in their own behalf. And if you're working with five, six, seven guys, you're the one that's going to speak up, you're gone, and they still got the job. You know. So you moderate that, try to be as diplomatic about it as possible.
But it didn't make for progress for what we're trying to do.
